title: Big plants on a slower clock
question: Which box looks more like a living stand of trees to you? Pick one — the numbers under each are real and both boxes are alive.
context_md:
You asked whether big plants could tick less often the bigger they get. Built: a plant waits longer between ticks by size (seedling every tick, a grown tree every fifth), and bending is off in both panes here.

**It works on the clock — 10 seeds, every one faster, median 2.7x, worst 1.7x.** What I cannot judge is whether it still looks like your box.

Same bed, same seed, same 64,000 frames. Four stops down each sheet: frames 8,000 / 24,000 / 48,000 / 64,000.

**What the change does to the stand, and it is not subtle:** roughly a third as many plants, slightly *more* plant material, and about **60% more leaf**. Fewer, bigger, much leafier trees. That held on all 10 seeds — every slow-clock run had more leaf than every normal run.

**What to ignore:** the speed. I am not asking which is faster, I know which is faster. I am asking whether the thinner, leafier box is one you would want to play in, or whether losing two-thirds of the individuals reads as an emptier world.

items.label: A — normal clock (current behaviour)
items.caption: every plant ticks at the same rate whatever its size

items.label: B — big plants on a slower clock
items.caption: a seedling ticks every time, a grown tree every fifth
